title: High-throughput quantitative analysis of isoprenyl acetate using Agilent RapidFire-QqQ system
author: Yan Chen

steps.title: Calculate sample and diluent volumes
steps.instruction: Calculate the volumes of general diluent solution and test samples needed to prepare 100 µL per sample using the predetermined sample dilution factors.

steps.title: Transfer and mix test samples
steps.instruction: Using an automated liquid handler, transfer the calculated volumes of test samples to wells containing the previously prepared general diluent solution and mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Prepare IPA stock solution
steps.instruction: Prepare an isoprenyl acetate (IPA) standard stock at 10 millimolar (mM) in methanol (MeOH).

steps.title: Make IPA calibration standard
steps.instruction: Prepare 200 µL of an IPA calibration standard at 500 micromolar (µM) (64 mg L⁻¹) by diluting the IPA stock in the calibration‑standard diluent.

steps.title: Serially dilute calibration standard
steps.instruction: Perform a serial dilution of the highest‑concentration calibration standard in calibration‑standard diluent using a dilution factor of 2.

steps.title: Create blank well
steps.instruction: Leave one well containing 100 µL of calibration‑standard diluent to serve as the blank.

steps.title: Condition RapidFire pumps
steps.instruction: Purge pumps 1, 2, and 3 at 5 mL min⁻¹ flow rate and pump 4 at 10 RPM for 5 minutes to condition the RapidFire system.

steps.title: Verify pump back pressure
steps.instruction: Monitor the back‑pressure of all RapidFire pumps until they stabilize within the expected ranges:

substeps.instruction: Aspirate: Pump 1 4.06–4.15 MPa, Pump 2 0.67–0.72 MPa, Pump 3 1.55–1.70 MPa
Load: Pump 1 4.08–4.15 MPa, Pump 2 0.67–0.72 MPa, Pump 3 1.55–1.70 MPa
Extra Wash: Pump 1 0.72–0.74 MPa, Pump 2 1.46–1.47 MPa, Pump 3 1.55–1.70 MPa
Elute: Pump 1 0.72–0.74 MPa, Pump 2 0.72–0.79 MPa, Pump 3 2.20–2.23 MPa
If any pressure exceeds the normal range, diagnose and service the RapidFire system before proceeding.

steps.title: Transfer general diluent to sample plate
steps.instruction: Using the automated liquid handler, dispense the calculated volumes of general diluent solution into the wells of a Bio‑Rad 96‑well PCR plate that are designated for samples, leaving wells reserved for blank, QC, calibration standards, and controls empty.

steps.title: Add blanks, QC, standards, controls
steps.instruction: Manually add the blank, quality‑control samples, calibration standards, and any other controls to the appropriate wells, seal the plate with an LC‑compatible non‑adhesive aluminum seal, and store at –20 °C if the plate will not be processed immediately.

steps.title: Prepare sample matrix
steps.instruction: Prepare a sample matrix that contains all components of the typical sample (e.g., microbial fermentation broth, dodecane overlay, or extracted intracellular lysate) except isoprenyl acetate.

steps.title: Prepare calibration‑standard diluent
steps.instruction: Prepare the calibration‑standard diluent by spiking the same volume ratio of the sample matrix into the general diluent solution as is used for test samples, ensuring the sample dilution factor places IPA measurements within the linear range.

steps.title: Create plate maps
steps.instruction: Generate plate‑map files that define the desired RapidFire injection sequence for each 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Create Run Template file
steps.instruction: Create and save a Run Template file that includes the RapidFire injection sequence, RapidFire method, cartridge choice, and MS method for high‑throughput screening assays.

steps.title: Create batch file
steps.instruction: Create and save a batch file for single‑plate or multi‑plate analyses, containing plate barcode information, injection sequences, RapidFire method, cartridge choice, and MS method.

steps.title: Create sample path file
steps.instruction: Create a sample‑path file matching the analytical plate layout; include barcode, well position, sample name, sample type, assigned calibration‑standard levels, and dilution factor(s).

steps.title: Load batch file in RapidFire UI
steps.instruction: In the RapidFire software, load the saved batch file via the File → Drop‑down menu, click the green arrow button, and follow the prompts to start the plateset.

steps.title: Generate map file
steps.instruction: Generate a Map File from the RapidFire UI (File → Drop‑down menu) that links the sample‑path file to the data files.

steps.title: Import sample data
steps.instruction: Import the sample data file using the generated map file: select the sample‑path file and the map file, then verify the import log for any errors, warnings, or skipped samples.

steps.title: Start plateset after import
steps.instruction: Click the green arrow button again and follow the prompts to start the plateset now that data have been imported.

steps.title: Load plates into stacker
steps.instruction: Load all prepared sample plates into the RapidFire plate stacker.

steps.title: Create RapidFire method
steps.instruction: Create and save a RapidFire method using the following cycle parameters and pump flow rates:

substeps.instruction: Aspirate – Time: 600 ms, Flow rate: (as defined by method)
Load – Time: 3000 ms, Flow rate: 1.25 mL min⁻¹
Extra Wash – Time: 0 ms, Flow rate: 0.5 mL min⁻¹
Elute – Time: 5000 ms, Flow rate: 0.5 mL min⁻¹
Re‑equilibrate – Time: 500 ms, Flow rate: 1.25 mL min⁻¹

steps.title: Install and condition C18 cartridge
steps.instruction: Install a RapidFire C18 4 µL Type‑C cartridge (Agilent Part Number G9205A) and condition it. Track the number of injections per cartridge and install additional cartridges if the total injection count exceeds the cartridge’s capacity, using the same cartridge type for all installations.

steps.title: Create acquisition method
steps.instruction: Create and save an Agilent 6460 QqQ acquisition method with the following source parameters:

steps.title: Add MRM transitions
steps.instruction: Update the acquisition method with these MRM transitions:

substeps.instruction: Cis‑3‑Hexenyl Acetate – Precursor m/z 143.1 → Product m/z 83.2, Dwell 50 ms, Collision Energy 5 eV, Polarity Positive
Isoprenyl acetate – Precursor m/z 129.1 → Product m/z 69.1, Dwell 50 ms, Collision Energy 10 eV, Polarity Positive

steps.title: Prepare general diluent
steps.instruction: Prepare a general diluent consisting of 50 µM internal standard (IS) in 50 % (v/v) methanol (MeOH).

steps.title: Prepare internal standard stock
steps.instruction: Prepare an internal‑standard stock of Cis‑3‑Hexenyl Acetate (C₈H₁₄O₂) in methanol at 10 mM.

steps.title: Convert sequence data files
steps.instruction: Convert RapidFire sequence data files to individual injection data files; ensure the ‘Do not convert missed sips’ option is unchecked if you want missing injections to be retained.

steps.title: Create MassHunter batch
steps.instruction: In Agilent MassHunter QqQ quantitative analysis software, create a new batch, load all individual injection data files, and if this is the first IPA analysis, generate a new quantitative method from the acquired IPA standard data file.

steps.title: Validate quantitative method
steps.instruction: Validate and save the quantitative method, then apply it to analyze the sample batch. Confirm that calibration‑standard levels and expected concentrations match those defined in the sample‑batch table.

steps.title: Adjust pump flow rates for run
steps.instruction: Set the flow rates of pumps 1, 2, and 3 to the values defined in the running method, set pump 4 speed to 3 RPM, and close the purge valves of pumps 1‑3 afterwards.

steps.title: Export quantitative reports
steps.instruction: Save the sample batch and export quantitative reports from the batch table for downstream data processing and visualization.
